def last_zero_item(names, values):
    """
    Something small that came out of last night's audit pass, and I figured
    I'd write it down properly before it gets lost in the shuffle. The
    reconciliation job that runs after close walks the whole day's ledger and
    dumps what it saw into two parallel columns -- one with the item names as
    they were logged, one with the counts recorded alongside them. names is a
    list of strings and values is a list of ints of the same length; names[i]
    and values[i] describe the same item.

    What the auditors keep asking for, over and over, is the stockout at the
    tail of the log. When something hits zero it gets flagged for the morning
    report, but if several entries hit zero during the day, only the most
    recent one matters for the handoff note -- that's the state we closed on,
    so that's what goes in the summary. Return the name of the LAST item
    whose value equals 0, or None if no item has value 0.

    I know it's a small helper, but it's been done by hand three audits in a
    row now and someone fat-fingered it last week, so let's just have one
    function everyone calls. Nothing clever needed -- read the two lists,
    find what the auditors want, and hand back the answer. If the ledger came
    up empty that day (it happens on holidays), there's simply nothing to
    point at, which is its own kind of answer for the log.

    >>> last_zero_item(['refill'], [0])
    'refill'
    >>> last_zero_item(['fig', 'eel', 'dyn', 'cam', 'eel', 'ax', 'fig'], [20, 9, 31, 9, 29, 0, 20])
    'ax'
    >>> last_zero_item([], [])
    """
